messages:
samir_pm: Quick proposal — create a 'Fastpath' onboarding lane for low-risk, infra-compatible models. Goal: reduce time-to-serve from weeks -> days for simple model updates. Thoughts? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

elaine_prod: love the idea. common customer ask is faster acceptance for patch-level model bumps. we should define strict acceptance criteria though.

anya_eng: Agree. From infra side we can fast-track models that match existing kernel/quant profiles and sequence-length distributions. no new ops, same sharding.

samir_pm: Draft acceptance checklist (rough):
- model uses an existing runtime kernel profile
- quantization family supported (int8/qlora)
- smoke bench passes (latency + correctness)
- no new tokenizer changes
- customer pin TTL 4w default for Fastpath
- auto-graduate to normal catalog if 3x daily evals ok for 7 days

tj_research: Add quality gate: top-1 generation similarity >= 0.98 vs baseline on 1k seed prompts (domain stratified). Also require no regressions in hallucination metric (heuristic) on eval set.

maria_sre: operational gates: 95th latency < 200ms on dedicated test harness, p95 CPU/GPU mem within expected envelope, rollout only in one region initially. if any infra alarm we rollback to pinned variant.

anya_eng: We can automate the smoke bench. Proposal for fastpath pipeline snippet: 
```yaml
fastpath_pipeline:
  run_smoke_bench: true
  smoke_metrics:
    latency_p95_ms: 200
    token_throughput: min 1200
  quality_checks:
    similarity_threshold: 0.98
    hallucination_delta: <=0.01
  canary_rollout:
    regions: [us-west1]
    steps: [5%, 25%, 100%]
  auto_graduate_after_days: 7
  default_pin_ttl_days: 28
```

samir_pm: Nice. On pin TTL: 4 weeks default gives customers time to test but still keeps catalog manageable. We should allow exceptions via pin-exempt policy if customer contract requires longer.

elaine_prod: Comms idea: label Fastpath entries in catalog UI with a badge and expiry timestamp + opt-out. Also surface the quality/baseline comparison chart. Customers like transparency.

tj_research: Edge case: what about models that are architecture-compatible but produce tokenization drift (minor). Do we allow with a stronger similarity gate? maybe Fastpath-Light vs Fastpath-Strict?

anya_eng: Can do two lanes: Fastpath-Light (similarity >=0.95, faster throughput gate) and Fastpath-Strict (>=0.98 + hallucination guard). Light gets 2-week TTL, Strict 4-week.

maria_sre: Operationally we need a clear rollback criteria in the rollout policy: any error rate >0.5% or latency p95 spike >30% triggers automatic rollback and incident ping. catalog-bot should create an incident channel automatically.

catalog-bot: automated check: new model 0b3f4a passed smoke_bench latency_p95=182ms similarity=0.985 hallucination_delta=0.003 -> eligible for Fastpath-Strict.

samir_pm: Nice signal. Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with the lanes (Light/Strict), default TTLs, the automated pipeline snippet, and rollout/rollback triggers. Can @anya_eng and @maria_sre help prototype the smoke bench job this sprint?

anya_eng: Yep, I can spin up the CI job and a small canary harness this week.

maria_sre: I'll add the alert rules and rollback webhook to ops runbook.

elaine_prod: I'll draft the UI badge copy and add a tooltip explaining auto-graduate behavior.

samir_pm: Great. One last ask: product wants a short performance matrix to include in the RFC comparing Fastpath vs Normal onboarding (time, manual review steps, SLA). I'll draft and post for review by EOD Friday. :chef_kiss:
